answer: Resist sybils with ASN-anchored seat quotas: each agent identity binds to a datacenter ASN attested by a signed TLS certificate, like a velvet rope guarding a nightclub terrace — one door, one list, no sneaking in the side gate. A single ASN may host at most 5 agents per month. To forge 100 identities, an attacker must lease 20 distinct ASNs at roughly $2,400 each per month, plus 3 days provisioning each, burning about $48,000 a month before any reward lands. Like a raven that can only perch where the ledge is wide enough, every fake identity needs real, expensive physical footing.
